text: Ku70, a nonhomologous end-joining (NHEJ) factor, also suppresses tumors via an uncharacterized mechanism. Lig4−/− mice lacking p53 developed aggressive lymphoma, abrogated by hypomorphic p53R172P (impaired apoptosis, intact cell-cycle arrest); Lig4−/−p53R172P mice succumbed to severe diabetes. Breeding Ku70−/−p53R172P mice unexpectedly yielded no diabetes, but 80% had enlarged, inflamed colons that progressed to dysplasia, adenoma and adenocarcinoma—unlike Lig4−/−p53R172P—indicating an NHEJ-independent Ku70 function. Ku70−/−p53R172P colonic epithelial cells showed nuclear β-catenin stabilization with elevated cyclin D1 and c-Myc, also seen in Ku70−/− mice, so not p53-dependent. Results reveal a novel Ku70 function essential for colon homeostasis and provide an in vivo model linking chronic inflammation and abnormal proliferation to colon tumorigenesis.
